question:
Choose the correct one-word substitution for:

"A person who is indifferent to pleasure or pain".
solution:
The correct answer is: **Stoic**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Stoic"** refers to a person who is indifferent to pleasure or pain, showing self-control and resilience in the face of adversity. (संवेदनहीन/सहिष्णु)

 
 
• **Example:** Despite losing everything in the fire, he remained stoic and focused on rebuilding his life.
 
 
 
• **"Indifferent to pleasure or pain"** means having an attitude where emotional highs and lows do not significantly affect the person. (आनंद और दर्द के प्रति उदासीन)
 
 
• **Example:** She was stoic during the funeral, offering comfort to others while hiding her own grief.
 
 
 
• Hence, the word that best fits the description is **"Stoic."**

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Stoic**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Epicure** (भोगवादी): A person who takes particular pleasure in fine food and drink.

 
 
• **Example:** The epicure spent hours choosing the perfect wine to complement his dinner.
 
 
 
• **Pessimist** (निराशावादी): A person who tends to see the worst aspect of things or believe that the worst will happen.
 
 
• **Example:** The pessimist was convinced that the project would fail, despite everyone's efforts.
 
 
 
• **Masochist** (स्वयं कष्ट उठाने वाला): A person who derives pleasure from their own pain or humiliation.
 
 
• **Example:** The masochist found satisfaction in enduring challenges that others avoided.
 
 

Q1: Choose the correct one-word substitution for: "A person who is indifferent to pleasure or pain."

The correct answer is: **Stoic**.
